correctness.rationale: For every inclusion-minimal Hall-deficient group \(Z\) of size \(z\), its neighborhood has exactly \(z-1\) houses. Removing it exhausts one highest remaining tier of each participating agent. Each agent belongs to at most \(k-1\) groups, since an agent on her final remaining tier sees every active house and cannot be Hall deficient while at least \(n\) houses remain. For \(T\) rounds, the removal count obeys \(R\le\min\{(n-1)T,n(k-1)-T\}\le(n-1)(k-1)\). Therefore \(m\ge k(n-1)+1\) leaves at least \(n\) houses and forces a saturating top-choice matching. Identical tiers each of size \(n-1\) give the sharp obstruction at \(m=k(n-1)\). Exhaustive small-domain and standalone randomized checks corroborate but do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The sharp uniform resource threshold quantifies exactly how many spare houses guarantee a zero-transfer envy-free allocation in any coarse ordinal market with at most \(k\) tiers per agent. Heterogeneous arbitrary weak preferences are allowed; the two-tier \(2n-1\) boundary and homogeneous impossibility witnesses are natural economic capacity results. A new cross-round structural invariant upgrades a known decision algorithm to a nontrivial exact universally quantified extremal theorem.
